plain_english_policy: This bill mandates that any education employee in Alabama (teachers on continuing service status, principals, contract principals, or nonprobationary employees) whose teaching certificate is revoked due to a felony conviction involving a child must have their employment immediately cancelled or terminated. The revocation applies specifically to convictions for listed sex offenses against children and other crimes endangering a child's welfare.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would produce an automatic, immediate loss of employment status for educators convicted of specific felonies involving minors (e.g., rape, sodomy, sexual abuse, child pornography), regardless of prior tenure or probationary status. It also establishes a mechanism to reinstate employees and provide back pay if the conviction is later overturned on appeal.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsors affirmatively advanced this bill requiring immediate termination of employment for educators convicted of felonies involving children.
evidence_quotes: This bill would require the State Superintendent of Education to revoke the teaching or other educational certificate of any person convicted of a felony or sex offense involving a child and would provide for the immediate cancellation of the employment contract or employment of any education employee convicted of a felony or sex offense involving a child.
